stem: The field suffers from being puffed up with its own importance, and that attitude of ____ seems to infect every professional utterance.
Stigler brings a fundamental (i)____ to his protagonists, somehow treating them with respect even while he reveals these sometimes prickly characters behaving in (ii)____ ways.

The (i)____ seen in most of eastern Eurasia is (ii)____ on the Mongolian plateau, despite only 200 millimeters of annual precipitation, because evaporation decreases at higher altitudes and latitudes.

William Newman and Lawrence Principe point out that prior to the seventeenth century the terms “alchemy” and “chemistry” were largely (i)____ in European usage. It was from the third decade of the eighteenth century that the two terms began to (ii)____. Newman and Principe suggest that a third term, “chymistry,” should be used to denote the transitional early modern phase when “alchemy and “chemistry” were becoming (iii)____.

In mid-twentieth-century Japanese monster movies, a giant creature typically attacks Japan and is ultimately vanquished either by some fortuitous scientific discovery or by another equally ____ plot device.

Strong chemical bonds and large energetic reactions are dramatic and easy to observe and understand, but a lot of the world around us and inside us operates on more ____ atomic and molecular interactions.
By 2004 the idiosyncratic building had become ____ part of the city's urban landscape— hence the outrage when its owners announced that they planned to destroy its facade as part of a renovation.
